title: Halifax NP719 Memorial, Nørreskov Forest, Als
location_name: Nørreskov forest, Als island, northeast of Elstrup, Sønderborg municipality, South Jutland, Denmark
cause_of_loss: Mid-air collision with Halifax MZ915 of 466 Squadron RAAF at 01:05 hours over Als island on return from Kiel; both aircraft lost
memorial_details: Memorial stone in Nørreskov forest replacing an original propeller-blade marker placed by local residents. Inscription reads 'RAF 19-9-1944' (commemorating the burial date). New memorial stones unveiled 16 September 2019 (75th anniversary). An information placard is installed at the memorial site. Annual ceremonies are held in the forest on the evening of 16 September. The ceremonies are civilian-led — not Danish Air Force events, as sometimes stated.
crew_summary: All seven killed. Initially buried in a mound in Nørreskov forest (marked with a propeller blade); formally buried Aabenraa Cemetery 18 September 1944; reinterred August 1946 under British Commonwealth War Graves arrangements.
narrative:
NP719 was one of fourteen 432 Squadron aircraft on the Kiel raid of 15/16 September 1944. Returning in darkness over the Baltic and southern Denmark, it collided with Halifax MZ915 of 466 Squadron RAAF at 01:05 hours over Als island. Both aircraft came down in or near Nørreskov forest. All fourteen airmen across the two crews were killed.

Danish civilians, led by local forester Angelo, recovered remains from the forest and formed a burial mound marked with a propeller blade. A Danish Army NCO School personnel member, L. Larsen, documented the scene. The dead were formally buried at Aabenraa on 18 September 1944, then disinterred in August 1946 for reburial under British Commonwealth War Graves arrangements at Aabenraa Cemetery.

The forest site passed into local memory. Annual ceremonies on 16 September became an established tradition — the flensted.eu.com Danish airwar database, which is the most detailed primary source for Danish crash sites, records these observances. The 75th anniversary in 2019 prompted the installation of new memorial stones.
contributor: Keith Binley, Bomber Command Memorial Register
community_connection: Local Danish civilian tradition maintained for over 75 years. Annual 16 September observances in Nørreskov forest, civilian-led. flensted.eu.com and airmen.dk document the site. Danish Army NCO School personnel documented the original recovery. New memorial stones installed for the 75th anniversary in 2019.
